correctness.rationale: Separable degree-n even branch polynomial gives smooth genus (n-2)/2 cover and eight rational points. Quadratic-character expansion counts simultaneous residue conditions; the elliptic trace on \(y^2=x^3-x\) is explicit; restriction to subfields and Möbius inversion produce exact polynomial formula; the proper-subfield bound proves positivity at all even n>=6. Two independent finite computations substantiate the finite numbers without being used as the infinite proof.

evidence: Faber--Grantham Theorem 2.4 establishes maximal eight-point count; Vermeulen Theorem 1.1 proves eventual maximal gonality point counts by toric methods but does not classify Frobenius branch orbits; Gao--Kuttner--Wang treats prescribed terminal or leading coefficient data; Slavov establishes varying-q asymptotic distributions in short intervals.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The broader max-eight-point existence result omits the single Frobenius orbit requirement. Coefficient and large-q factorization statements have distinct hypotheses and do not give this fixed-F3 all-n closed count as printed. General arithmetic-progression theory is an explicit residual priority risk.

evidence: A degree-n single Frobenius branch point is equivalent to an irreducible branch polynomial; all four rational hyperelliptic fibres split iff the polynomial evaluates to 1 at 0,1,-1 and is monic.

originality.rationale: The max-eight-point assertion and genus-two examples are explicitly prior; the new comparison target is the simultaneous all-genus one-orbit branch condition and precise ternary arithmetic-progression count. Accessible primary papers on point maximization, prescribed polynomial coefficients, and short-interval factorization lack this combined fixed-F3 formula. A classical general arithmetic-progression count may conceivably specialize to it, and this remains a priority risk, but no inspected explicit statement implies the joint theorem without a new calculation.
residual_risks: A classical Dirichlet-character/L-function arithmetic-progression formula may imply this specialization after computing its nontrivial characters; no claim of universal novelty is justified.
Unindexed earlier branch-transitivity constructions or exact low-field tables may exist.
Existing genus-two classifications cover the g=2 examples and those are not asserted as new.

value.rationale: The natural entire Weierstrass branch locus of a maximally rational hyperelliptic cover is made Frobenius-transitive in every genus. Exact counts for irreducible full branch divisors distinguish this arithmetic geometry from arbitrary maximal-point covers; the all-genus existence is a structural refinement of an established sharp problem rather than an isolated computation.
